results.note: Synopsis chronica: Searched extensively; no English translation located. This is a brief chronicle text (506 words) that does not appear in major translation collections.

Dissertatio ad Liberatum: Searched multiple times with no results. This appears to be a scholarly dissertation in the PL itself, not a primary patristic text, unlikely to have a standalone English translation.

Computus Paschalis: A technical text on Easter calculation; searches found explanations of computus but no specific English translation of this work. Appears to be technical/scientific rather than hagiographic material.

Cassiodori supplementum: Searched for Cassiodorus supplement materials; found no specific English translation. Cassiodorus's Variae and Institutiones exist in English, but this supplementary text does not.
Prosa de S. Martino: No English translation located. Searches returned results for Italian poetry about Saint Martin but not this medieval prose work.
Relatio: No English translation found. This brief text (416 words) does not appear in major hagiographic collections or translation databases.

Vita S. Pachomii: Public-domain English translation in Helen Waddell's The Desert Fathers (1936), available at vitae-patrum.org.uk and Internet Archive. Also translated by A.N. Athanassakis (copyrighted, 1975) and A. Veilleux (copyrighted, 1980).
Verba seniorum (version 1): Richard J. Goodrich, The Desert Fathers: Verba Seniorum III, VI, and VII, Ancient Christian Writers vol. 74 (2020); also Helen Waddell translation (1936, pd-ingested).
Verba seniorum (version 2): Same as 3000—Goodrich (copyrighted 2020); Waddell (pd-ingested, 1936).
Verba seniorum (version 3): Helen Waddell's The Desert Fathers (1936) contains the Sayings of the Fathers; public-domain translation available at vitae-patrum.org.uk and Internet Archive.
Vita S. Ephraem: J.P. Amar, Ed., The Syriac «Vita» Tradition of Ephrem the Syrian (Louvain: Peeters, 2011); bilingual edition with critical manuscripts.

Vita B. Posthumii: Likely included in Helen Waddell's The Desert Fathers (1936) based on vitae-patrum.org.uk catalog references, but not explicitly confirmed in search results. Possibly public-domain via Waddell if present.
Vita S. Eugeniae: Helen Waddell's The Desert Fathers (1936, pd-ingested); also Ælfric of Eynsham's Old English translation (medieval, pd); Caxton's Golden Legend includes Saint Eugenia.

Vita S. Euphrasiae: Helen Waddell's The Desert Fathers (1936, pd-ingested); also MLA publication of Old French verse version with English translation (2000s), though original Latin translation status varies.

Vita S. Euphrosunae: MLA publication 'The Life of Saint Eufrosine: In Old French Verse with English Translation' mentioned in search results; unclear if Latin original also translated or only Old French version.
Vita S. Frontonii: Helen Waddell's The Desert Fathers (1936) appears to include this life based on vitae-patrum.org.uk references; pd-ingested translation.
Vita S. Marinae: Helen Waddell's The Desert Fathers (1936, pd-ingested); also Caxton's Golden Legend translation (14th-15th century, pd).
Vita S. Thaisis: Helen Waddell's The Desert Fathers (1936, pd-ingested); also medieval English versions in Northern Homily Collection and TEAMS editions (pd).
Vita SS. Epicteti et Astionis: No English translation located. Related text 'Passio Epicteti Presbyteri et Astionis Monachi' mentioned in obscure contexts but no translation found.
Vita S. Abrahae: Helen Waddell's The Desert Fathers (1936, pd-ingested); available at vitae-patrum.org.uk page 17.

Vita S. Mariae meretricis: Benedicta Ward, Harlots of the Desert: A Study of Repentance in Early Monastic Sources (Cistercian Studies Series 106); contains translations of Mary the Harlot and related lives.
Vita S. Onuphrii: Helen Waddell's The Desert Fathers (1936, pd-ingested) appears to include this life based on search results mentioning Onuphrius in Waddell context.

Aegyptiorum patrum sententiae: Associated with Martin of Braga's collection (PL 74:381-394); covered by Waddell and other desert fathers collections but specific status of this particular compilation unclear.
Heraclidis Paradisus: Extensively searched; no English translation located. This work (Heracleides the Hermit, 4th-5th century) exists in Latin but not in modern English translation.
De Historia Lausiaca Palladii: W.K. Lowther Clarke translation (1918, likely pd—available on Tertullian.org); John Wortley, The Lausiac History (Cistercian Studies Series, copyrighted).
Appendix ad epistolas: Very brief text (141 words) in epistolary collection context; no English translation found. Likely editorial apparatus rather than primary text.
Divisio geographica epistolarum: Searched extensively; no English translation located. This appears to be an organizational index rather than primary patristic material.
Ordo restitutus epistolarum cum antea vulgato comparatus: No English translation found. This comparative editorial work on epistolary ordering does not appear in major translation collections.
Ordo restitutus epistolarum: No English translation located. This appears to be editorial apparatus for ordering epistles, not a primary patristic text.
Ordo vetus epistolarum cum novo comparatus: No English translation found. This is comparative editorial material, not a primary theological work.
Admonitio in Ordinem Romanum XV: Searched extensively; no English translation located. This brief (281 words) liturgical admonition does not appear in translation collections.
Appendix (spanning volumes 78, 87): Editorial appendix material; no English translation found. Likely supplementary scholarly apparatus rather than primary patristic text.
Ordo Romanus I: Multiple English translations available—E.G. Cuthbert Atchley (1905, likely pd); Alan Griffiths, Ordo Romanus Primus (2012, copyrighted, Joint Liturgical Studies 73).
Ordo Romanus II: Covered by Alan Griffiths's comprehensive translation of the Ordines Romani (2012, copyrighted). Atchley 1905 edition also available (likely pd).
Ordo Romanus III: Covered by Griffiths (2012, copyrighted) and Atchley (1905, likely pd) translations.
Ordo Romanus IV: Covered by Griffiths (2012, copyrighted) and Atchley (1905, likely pd) translations.
Ordo Romanus IX: Covered by Griffiths (2012, copyrighted) and Atchley (1905, likely pd) translations of the Ordines Romani.
Ordo Romanus V: Covered by Griffiths (2012, copyrighted) and Atchley (1905, likely pd) translations.
Ordo Romanus VI: Covered by Griffiths (2012, copyrighted) and Atchley (1905, likely pd) translations.
Ordo Romanus VII: Covered by Griffiths (2012, copyrighted) and Atchley (1905, likely pd) translations.
Ordo Romanus VIII: Covered by Griffiths (2012, copyrighted) and Atchley (1905, likely pd) translations.
Ordo Romanus X: Covered by Griffiths (2012, copyrighted) and Atchley (1905, likely pd) translations.
Ordo Romanus XVI: Covered by Griffiths (2012, copyrighted) and Atchley (1905, likely pd) translations of the Ordines Romani.
Testimonium: Brief text (269 words) that appears to be editorial attestation material in the PL itself; no English translation found.
De visione Taionis: Searched extensively; no English translation located. This 7th-century vision text about Bishop Taio exists in Latin original and Spanish scholarship but not in modern English.
